brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Organism metaphor reads instantly — green calm cell vs orange agitated cell creates strong emotional/semantic mapping to system state
Restrained palette and generous negative space let the glowing nuclei carry visceral weight without UI chrome competing
Typographic hierarchy is clean: oversized percent, quiet caps labels, and a tertiary metadata line in a coherent rhythm
dominant_weaknesses: Only two organisms shown — disk, GPU, network are absent on the canvas, making the 'system' feel half-built despite footer stats
Footer bar is visually disconnected: lighter background, different type treatment, and cramped metric grid breaks the dark organism stage
Static screenshot under-communicates the breathing/pulsing behavior central to the brief; orbit dots feel decorative rather than data-bound
fix_priorities: Bind orbit particles and pulse rate to real metrics (frequency = load) so motion is legible data, not ambient decoration
Expand to 4–6 organisms in a coherent grid so the 'ecosystem' premise holds
Unify footer with the dark stage — same background, lighter dividers, aligned baseline grid
Add subtle status microcopy near each organism (heart-rate, respiration) to reinforce the metaphor reflectively
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective pull from the organism metaphor, but behavioral utility is thin — you can't tell which process is stressed or act on it.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes, the breathing/pulsing organism concept is legible at a glance, though the execution shows the metaphor more than it operationalizes it.
